There is deliberately no recovery-code fallback, because confirming must prove the authenticator app holds the secret. The accepted step is remembered, so the code that confirmed enrollment cannot be replayed against the first challenge inside its window. Implemented at `TwoFactorAuthenticator.cs:90`.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by `TwoFactorAuthenticator` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Auth/TwoFactor/TwoFactorAuthenticator.cs`), called from `AuthenticationServiceBase.cs` (2 sites), from `ConfirmTwoFactorEnrollmentHandlerBase.cs:83` (`VerifyEnrollmentCodeAsync`), and by the disable and recovery-code regeneration handler bases, and registered in `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.Auth.cs`.

### ITwoFactorSecretProtector
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Auth.TwoFactor` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/TwoFactor/ITwoFactorSecretProtector.cs:13` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: protects an account's two-factor shared secret at rest, so the app's [ITwoFactorStore](#itwofactorstore) only ever holds the protected form.
- **Depends on**: `Result<T>`.
- **Concept**: encryption at rest behind a two-method port. Per the interface summary (`ITwoFactorSecretProtector.cs:5-12`), the enrollment workflow protects the freshly minted secret before it reaches the store, and the shipped [ITwoFactorAuthenticator](#itwofactorauthenticator) unprotects the stored value when it verifies a code.
- **Walkthrough**: `Protect(secret)` (line 18) turns the plaintext Base32 secret into its stored form. `Unprotect(protectedSecret)` (line 23) returns `Result<string>` and never throws: a failure means this host's key ring cannot read the value.
- **Why it's built this way**: a database leak alone then yields no usable TOTP secret. The default uses the host's data-protection key ring (summary lines 9-10), so a multi-replica host needs a shared key ring, and the `Result` return turns a key-ring mismatch into a handled failure instead of an exception in the sign-in path.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [DataProtectionTwoFactorSecretProtector](#dataprotectiontwofactorsecretprotector) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Auth/TwoFactor/DataProtectionTwoFactorSecretProtector.cs:15`) and registered as a singleton in `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.Auth.cs:59`; called by `BeginTwoFactorEnrollmentHandlerBase.cs` (protect) and [TwoFactorAuthenticator](#twofactorauthenticator) (unprotect); exercised end to end in `TwoFactorSecretProtectionEndToEndTests.cs`.

### ITwoFactorStore
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Auth.TwoFactor` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/TwoFactor/ITwoFactorStore.cs:24` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the persistence abstraction for one account's two-factor state: enrollment lifecycle, recovery-code replacement, and single recovery-code consumption.
- **Depends on**: `UserIdentifierType`, `ITwoFactorUserState` (the read shape, taught elsewhere in this group), `Result`.
- **Concept**: a two-phase enrollment (start, then complete) so an abandoned setup cannot lock an account out; the same two-phase shape a reader has already seen in other enrollment-style flows in this group.
- **Walkthrough**: `GetAsync(userId, cancellationToken)` (`ITwoFactorStore.cs:34`) returns `null` only when the account itself does not exist; an account that never enrolled still returns a state with `IsTwoFactorEnabled = false`. `StartEnrollmentAsync(userId, secret, cancellationToken)` (line 47) stores a freshly minted secret WITHOUT activating the factor, per its summary (lines 36-39), so an abandoned enrollment cannot lock the user out. The `secret` (param doc lines 41-44) arrives already in its protected form ([ITwoFactorSecretProtector](#itwofactorsecretprotector)); the store keeps it as given and returns it unchanged from `GetAsync`. `CompleteEnrollmentAsync(userId, recoveryCodeHashes, cancellationToken)` (lines 57-60) activates the factor and stores the first recovery-code hashes, called only after a code from the stored secret has verified. `DisableAsync(userId, cancellationToken)` (line 69) turns the factor off and clears the secret and recovery codes, so a later re-enrollment starts from a fresh secret. `ReplaceRecoveryCodesAsync(userId, recoveryCodeHashes, cancellationToken)` (lines 79-82) replaces the whole set, never appends, since regeneration exists to invalidate a list the user believes compromised. `ConsumeRecoveryCodeAsync(userId, recoveryCodeHash, cancellationToken)` (lines 96-99) removes one hash to spend it, and its remarks (lines 87-91) flag this as security-critical: it must persist before the sign-in it authorized is answered, or the same code could sign in twice.
- **Why it's built this way**: splitting `StartEnrollmentAsync`/`CompleteEnrollmentAsync` prevents a half-finished enrollment from ever becoming an active, un-verified second factor.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by the consuming app, not by Common: `AddTwoFactorAuthentication` deliberately registers no `ITwoFactorStore` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.Auth.cs:31`), and registering one alongside that call arms the sign-in challenge (line 37). Called by [TwoFactorAuthenticator](#twofactorauthenticator), by the enrollment/disable/regenerate handler bases in `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/TwoFactor/`, and by `TwoFactorControllerBase` and `UsersAdminControllerBase` in `MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.API/Controllers/`.

### IViewAsService
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Auth.ViewAs` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/IViewAsService.cs:10` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the view-as workflow contract: start a grant and mint its token, end a grant, and check whether a token's grant is still live.
- **Depends on**: [ViewAsGrantResponse](#viewasgrantresponse), `UserIdentifierType`, `Result`.
- **Concept**: read-only support access ([ADR-137](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/137-read-only-view-as-support-access.html)): a staff user gets a short-lived token whose `sub` is the viewed account, while the `act_sub` and `vag` claims name the staff user and the grant row behind it.
- **Walkthrough**: `StartAsync(staffUserId, targetUserId, reason, cancellationToken)` (`IViewAsService.cs:22-26`) grants and mints; its summary (lines 12-16) lists the refusals (the caller themselves, a missing or soft-deleted account, an account that itself holds `users:view-as`) and the reason must be 10 to 500 characters. `EndAsync(grantId, staffUserId, cancellationToken)` (line 33) ends the staff user's grant so its token is refused on the next request, answering not found when the staff user holds no such grant. `IsGrantActiveAsync(grantId, staffUserId, targetUserId, cancellationToken)` (lines 44-48) is true while the grant exists, names this staff user and this account, was not ended, and has not expired.
- **Why it's built this way**: every view-as request is re-checked against the grant row, so ending a grant takes effect immediately rather than when the token expires.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by [ViewAsService](#viewasservice), registered in `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:198`; `IsGrantActiveAsync` is called per request by `ViewAsGuardMiddleware` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.API/Middleware/ViewAsGuardMiddleware.cs:137`), and the start and end endpoints live on `UsersAdminControllerBase` and `AuthControllerBase`.

### IViewAsGrantStore
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Auth.ViewAs` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/IViewAsGrantStore.cs:11` · Level 4 · interface

- **What it is**: the persistence port for [ViewAsGrant](#viewasgrant) rows, the audit record of every staff view.
- **Depends on**: [ViewAsGrant](#viewasgrant), [ViewAsGrantListRequest](#viewasgrantlistrequest), `UserIdentifierType`.
- **Concept**: a purpose-built store interface rather than the generic repository, because the grant table is mapped only on the host that holds it (see [ViewAsSettings](#viewassettings)).
- **Walkthrough**: `AddAsync(grant, ...)` (`IViewAsGrantStore.cs:17`) inserts and saves. `FindAsync(grantId, ...)` (line 23) reads one row by the token's `vag` id. `EndAsync(grantId, staffUserId, endedAt, ...)` (line 34) puts the staff user in the lookup so one staff user cannot end another's grant, and returns true when the grant was found, ended now or before. `GetRecentForTargetAsync(targetUserId, maxCount, ...)` (lines 41-44) returns the newest grants on one account. `DeleteIssuedBeforeAsync(cutoff, ...)` (line 50) is the retention sweep and returns the row count. `ListAsync(request, now, ...)` (lines 62-65) pages the whole support access log newest first; its summary (lines 52-57) notes the status filter is evaluated at `now`, email filters compare case-insensitively against the display snapshots, and the page size is clamped to `ViewAsGrantListRequest.MaxPageSize`. `ForgetUserAsync(userId, ...)` (line 76) is the account-erasure step that blanks the display snapshot on every grant naming the account and, per lines 67-72, saves nothing itself: the erasure's own unit-of-work save persists it.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the erasure step unsaved lets it commit atomically with the rest of the account deletion.
- **Where it's used**: implemented by `EFViewAsGrantStore` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Auth/EFViewAsGrantStore.cs:36`, registered at `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:197`) and the test double `InMemoryViewAsGrantStore` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing/Support/InMemoryViewAsGrantStore.cs:13`). Called by [ViewAsService](#viewasservice), [SignInHistory](#signinhistory) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/Sessions/SignInHistory.cs:55`), `DeleteUserHandlerBase` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/DeleteUser/DeleteUserHandlerBase.cs:187`) and `ViewAsGrantsAdminControllerBase` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.API/Controllers/Administration/ViewAsGrantsAdminControllerBase.cs:76`).

### ViewAsGrantLogQuery
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Auth.ViewAs` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsGrantLogQuery.cs:12` · Level 4 · class

- **What it is**: a static helper that applies the support-access-log filters to any `IQueryable<ViewAsGrant>`.
- **Depends on**: [ViewAsGrant](#viewasgrant), [ViewAsGrantListRequest](#viewasgrantlistrequest), [ViewAsGrantStatus](#viewasgrantstatus).
- **Concept**: one filter definition shared by the EF store and the in-memory test double, so the two cannot drift.
- **Walkthrough**: `Filter(grants, request, now)` (`ViewAsGrantLogQuery.cs:26`) null-checks and composes the three private steps with AND (line 31), returning an unordered query. `ByEmail` (line 34) folds each needle with `ViewAsGrant.NormalizeDisplay` and applies a contains match against `StaffDisplay` and `TargetDisplay`. `ByWindow` (line 49) keeps `GrantedAt >= From` and `GrantedAt < To` (inclusive start, exclusive end). `ByStatus` (line 64) derives `Live` (not ended, `ExpiresAt > now`), `Ended` (`EndedAt` set) and `Expired` (not ended, `ExpiresAt <= now`) at lines 67-69, mirroring `ViewAsGrant.StatusAt`; no status means no filter.
- **Why it's built this way**: expressing the status as a translatable predicate keeps the filter in SQL on the EF path instead of materializing the log.
- **Where it's used**: `EFViewAsGrantStore.ListAsync` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Auth/EFViewAsGrantStore.cs:131`) and `InMemoryViewAsGrantStore` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing/Support/InMemoryViewAsGrantStore.cs:73`).

### ViewAsService
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Auth.ViewAs` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsService.cs:42` · Level 9 · class

- **What it is**: the shipped [IViewAsService](#iviewasservice): validates and audits a view-as grant, mints its token, ends it, and answers the per-request liveness check.
- **Depends on**: [IViewAsGrantStore](#iviewasgrantstore), [ITokenService](#itokenservice), [IPermissionRegistry](#ipermissionregistry), [ViewAsSettings](#viewassettings), `TimeProvider`, and the optional [IViewAsSubjectResolver](#iviewassubjectresolver) and [ICurrentUserService](#icurrentuserservice) (`ViewAsService.cs:43-49`).
- **Concept introduced**: impersonation without identity theft. The minted token is an ordinary access token for the viewed account plus two claims, [AuthClaimTypes](#authclaimtypes).`ViewAsActor` and `ViewAsGrant` (lines 104-108); the command pipeline's ViewAs decorator and the guard middleware use them to keep the session read-only and tied to a live grant ([ADR-137](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/137-read-only-view-as-support-access.html)). `[Rubric §11, Security]` (assesses how the design limits and audits privileged access): every view is bounded in time, written to an audit row before a token exists, and refused for accounts that would give lateral or machine access.
- **Walkthrough**: `Lifetime` (lines 55-58) is the configured access-token lifetime when it is positive and below `ViewAsGrant.MaxLifetime`, otherwise `MaxLifetime` (the summary says 15 minutes), so a view never outlives an ordinary sign-in token. `StartAsync` (line 66) first validates self-view and the reason through `ViewAsGrant.Create` (line 76), returns `ViewAs.NotConfigured` when no resolver is registered (lines 82-87), then reads the subject (line 89) and runs `Refuse` (line 90). It rebuilds the grant with the display snapshots (line 99: the staff email from `StaffEmail`, the viewed email from the subject), sweeps rows older than `RetentionDays` (line 101) and adds the grant (line 102) BEFORE minting the token with `GenerateShortLivedAccessToken` (lines 109-115). `EndAsync` (line 121) answers `ViewAs.GrantNotFound` when the store found nothing (line 128). `IsGrantActiveAsync` (line 132) requires the row to exist, match both user ids and be active at now (lines 140-143). `StaffEmail` (line 153) reads the email claim (mapped `ClaimTypes.Email`, then raw `email`, line 161) only when the current user IS the staff user (line 155). `Refuse` (line 165) answers in order: not found (line 169), deleted (lines 172-174), service account per [ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html) (lines 178-180), locked (lines 187-189), and an account whose role holds `AdministrationPermissions.ViewAsUsers` (lines 193-194), so there is no lateral access.
- **Why it's built this way**: the remarks (lines 61-65) state the two ordering choices: the row is written before the token so no token exists without its audit record, and the retention sweep rides on grants (which are rare) instead of a hosted service in every process.
- **Where it's used**: registered scoped in `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/DependencyInjection.cs:198`; tested in `MMCA.Common/Tests/Core/MMCA.Common.Application.Tests/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsServiceTests.cs`, `ViewAsTokenTests.cs` and `ViewAsGuardMiddlewareTests.cs`.
- **Caveats / not-in-source**: the exact value of `ViewAsGrant.MaxLifetime` is stated here from the summary at lines 51-54, not re-read from `ViewAsGrant`.

### IPasswordHasher
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Interfaces.Infrastructure.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/IPasswordHasher.cs:6` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: the password-security port. Two required methods: hash a plaintext password into a separated `(byte[] Hash, byte[] Salt)` pair, and verify a plaintext against a stored hash plus salt. Two defaulted members follow: `NeedsRehash` lets the caller ask whether a hash that has just verified was derived with older parameters, and `BurnVerificationCost` spends one throwaway derivation on a sign-in branch that never reaches a real verification.
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party, BCL only (`byte[]`). Its Infrastructure adapter is [PasswordHasher](#passwordhasher).
- **Concept introduced: hash and salt kept apart.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses credential handling. Returning the hash and the salt as two distinct `byte[]` members (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/IPasswordHasher.cs:11`) rather than one concatenated blob keeps the storage contract explicit: the caller persists two columns, and `VerifyPassword` (`:18`) is unambiguous about what it re-derives and compares. Because the algorithm and its parameters live entirely behind this interface, they can be strengthened without touching a single Application handler ([ADR-032](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/032-password-hashing.html) sets the current hashing policy, applied inside [PasswordHasher](#passwordhasher)).
- **Walkthrough**: `(byte[] Hash, byte[] Salt) HashPassword(string password)` (`:11`) returns a named value tuple the caller stores as two fields. `bool VerifyPassword(string password, byte[] hash, byte[] salt)` (`:18`) re-derives from the supplied salt and compares. `bool NeedsRehash(byte[] hash) => false` (`:28`) is a default interface method: it answers whether the stored hash was derived with a format or work factor other than the one `HashPassword` uses now, and the `false` default keeps a custom hasher compiling without ever triggering a rehash. `void BurnVerificationCost(string password) => _ = HashPassword(password)` (`:39`) is the second default member, and its doc comment (`:30-37`) names the attack it closes: an unknown address or an account with no password never reaches `VerifyPassword`, so without a burn those branches would answer measurably faster than a wrong password. The burn must cost what verifying the **most expensive** stored record costs, so a hasher that still verifies records derived at an older, higher work factor overrides it to burn at that factor; the default (one `HashPassword`, discarded) is right only for a hasher whose every record uses its current parameters. `[Rubric §11, Security]` applies directly: this is user-enumeration resistance by timing, expressed as a contract member rather than left to each caller. The interface still declares no iteration count, algorithm identifier, or format version: the concrete decides what "current" means ([PasswordHasher](#passwordhasher) overrides `NeedsRehash` at `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Auth/PasswordHasher.cs:127`; [ADR-133](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/133-versioned-password-hash-work-factor.html) records the versioned work factor).
- **Why it's built this way**: a small port is the `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` dependency-inversion story in miniature. Swapping the key-derivation function or raising the iteration count is an Infrastructure change, invisible to the register, login, and change-password use cases that only ever see this contract. `NeedsRehash` closes the loop on such a change: existing records upgrade on their next successful sign-in, while the verified plaintext is still in hand, instead of staying on the old parameters forever.
- **Where it's used**: a primary-constructor dependency of [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser), which calls `VerifyPassword` on the login path (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:212`), `HashPassword` on registration (`:335`), `BurnVerificationCost` on the branches that have no credential to verify (`:965`), and, after tokens are issued, `NeedsRehash` then `HashPassword` in its best-effort rehash step (`:1016` and `:1021`) when the app's `User` implements [IPasswordRehashableUser](#ipasswordrehashableuser); into the shared [ChangePasswordHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#changepasswordhandlerbasetuser-tcommand), which verifies the current password (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/ChangePassword/ChangePasswordHandlerBase.cs:108`) before hashing the new one (`:118`); into [ResetPasswordHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#resetpasswordhandlerbasetuser-tcommand), which hashes the replacement after the token redeems (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/ResetPassword/ResetPasswordHandlerBase.cs:110`); and into the per-app Identity services, handlers and seeders that derive from those, for example ADC's [AuthenticationService](group-24-identity-module.md#authenticationservice) (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/Users/AuthenticationService.cs:54`), its `ChangePasswordHandler` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/Users/UseCases/ChangePassword/ChangePasswordHandler.cs:26`) and its module seeder (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.API/IdentityModuleSeeder.cs:34`, which needs the hasher because seed data carries plaintext credentials).

### ISoftDeletedUserValidator
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Interfaces.Infrastructure.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/ISoftDeletedUserValidator.cs:7` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: a single-method port that answers "has this account been soft-deleted?", called after JWT authentication to reject a soft-deleted user who still holds a valid, unexpired token (BR-133, named in the type comment at `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/ISoftDeletedUserValidator.cs:4`).
- **Depends on**: BCL plus the solution-wide `UserIdentifierType` alias (`:15`). See [primer §2](00-primer.md#2-architectural-styles-this-codebase-commits-to) for the alias convention and [ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html) for soft-delete versus erasure. The generic implementation is [SoftDeletedUserValidator<TUser>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#softdeleteduservalidatortuser).
- **Concept introduced: closing the stateless-token window.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses whether revocation is timely. A JWT is stateless: once signed it stays valid until `exp`, even if the account behind it was deleted a minute later. This port lets middleware re-ask the question on every authenticated request and fail the request when the answer is yes, with no per-handler code. The comment at `:5` states the second motive: the interface is declared in Application and implemented against the app's own `User` aggregate precisely so the middleware never takes a cross-module domain reference. That is the same dependency inversion as the other ports in this group, applied to a cross-module read.
- **Walkthrough**: one member, `Task<bool> IsUserSoftDeletedAsync(UserIdentifierType userId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)` (`:15`). One question, one answer, cancellable.
- **Where it's used**: [SoftDeletedUserMiddleware](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#softdeletedusermiddleware) resolves it lazily from the request scope (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.API/Middleware/SoftDeletedUserMiddleware.cs:117` calls `context.RequestServices.GetService<ISoftDeletedUserValidator>()`, so a host that registers no implementation simply skips the check; the reason is stated at `:43`) and queries it on a cache miss (`:113-115`). Both apps register the shared generic against their own user type: `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:43` and `MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.Store.Identity.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:43`, both as `TryAddScoped<ISoftDeletedUserValidator, SoftDeletedUserValidator<User>>()`.

### ITokenService
> MMCA.Common.Application · `MMCA.Common.Application.Interfaces.Infrastructure.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/ITokenService.cs:8` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: the token-minting port called by the login and refresh use cases. It builds a signed JWT access token from explicit identity facts (with a short-lived variant whose lifetime the caller chooses), generates an opaque refresh token, publishes the two token lifetimes, and recovers the `ClaimsPrincipal` from an expired-but-validly-signed access token.
- **Depends on**: `System.Security.Claims` (BCL, `:1`) and the `UserIdentifierType` alias. Its Infrastructure adapter is [TokenService](#tokenservice), which signs with the RSA key surfaced by [IJwksProvider](#ijwksprovider); [SessionStampingTokenService](#sessionstampingtokenservice) is a second, internal implementation that decorates the first.
- **Concept introduced: token creation as an Infrastructure detail.** `[Rubric §3, Clean Architecture]` assesses whether library-specific types stay out of the inner layers: the handlers call this contract and never see `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt`. `GetPrincipalFromExpiredToken` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/ITokenService.cs:75`) is the linchpin of the refresh flow: it validates the signature while deliberately ignoring lifetime, so an expired access token can still identify the user whose tokens are being rotated, returning `null` when the token is invalid (`:74`).
- **Walkthrough**: `GenerateAccessToken(UserIdentifierType userId, string email, string role, string fullName, IEnumerable<Claim>? additionalClaims = null)` (`:17-22`) takes the minimum claim set as typed parameters rather than a ready-made principal, with an escape hatch for module-specific claims. `GenerateShortLivedAccessToken(..., IEnumerable<Claim>? additionalClaims, TimeSpan lifetime)` (`:42-49`) is the same mint with an explicit expiry, written for the read-only view-as token, which must never outlive its 15-minute grant ([ADR-137](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/137-read-only-view-as-support-access.html), summary at `:24-28`). It is a **default interface member** that forwards to `GenerateAccessToken` and ignores `lifetime`, so a hand-written token service keeps compiling; the remarks (`:29-34`) explain why that default is still safe: the view-as guard checks the grant's own expiry on every request, so a longer-lived token is refused once its grant ([ViewAsGrant](#viewasgrant)) expires. `GenerateRefreshToken()` (`:53`) returns a cryptographically random base64 string. Two more default members publish the lifetimes: `AccessTokenLifetime` (`:60`, defaulting to 15 minutes) and `RefreshTokenLifetime` (`:67`, defaulting to 7 days), both documented as the BR-205 baseline. The comments at `:55-59` and `:62-66` explain the split: the real implementation derives both from the bound JWT settings, so the expiry reported to a client matches the token's actual `exp`, while the defaults keep hand-written test doubles on the baseline instead of forcing every double to implement two more members. That derivation is visible in the concrete: `TimeSpan.FromMinutes(_jwtSettings.AccessTokenExpirationMinutes)` and `TimeSpan.FromDays(_jwtSettings.RefreshTokenExpirationDays)` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Auth/TokenService.cs:192` and `:129`). `GetPrincipalFromExpiredToken(string token)` (`:75`) closes the set.
- **Why it's built this way**: the explicit-parameter overload is a `[Rubric §11, Security]` guardrail. The token's contents are a deliberate list, not whatever claims happened to ride in on an inbound principal. Surfacing the lifetimes through the same port removes the duplication where a caller would hard-code an expiry that could drift from the signed `exp`. Adding `GenerateShortLivedAccessToken` as a defaulted member rather than a required one follows the same rule as the lifetimes: a new capability on a shared port must not break the hand-written implementations and doubles consumers already have.
- **Where it's used**: [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser) reads the expired principal on refresh (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:415`) through its `TokenService` property, which exposes a *wrapped* instance to subclasses. [AuthSessionIssuer](#authsessionissuer) mints the refresh token when it opens a session (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/Sessions/AuthSessionIssuer.cs:476`) and when it rotates one (`:520`), and its wrapping implementation forwards `GenerateRefreshToken` and `GetPrincipalFromExpiredToken` to the inner service (`:796-800`). The short-lived mint has two callers: [ViewAsService](#viewasservice) for the view-as token (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsService.cs:109`, its lifetime capped at `ViewAsGrant.MaxLifetime`, `:56-58`) and [MachineClientService](#machineclientservice) for the client-credentials token (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/MachineClients/MachineClientService.cs:109`, [ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)). Each app's Identity service mints access tokens from the base's `TokenService` property, for example `MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Application/Users/AuthenticationService.cs` (access token plus the `speaker_id` claim). The rotated pair produced here is what [CookieSessionRefresher](#cookiesessionrefresher) later exchanges on the browser's behalf.

### ITwoFactorUserState
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/ITwoFactorUserState.cs:27` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: the two-factor enrollment surface an Identity module's `User` aggregate exposes: whether the second factor is active, the shared secret the codes are derived from (in protected form), and the hashes of the account's unspent recovery codes (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/ITwoFactorUserState.cs:29-43`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party beyond the BCL `IReadOnlyCollection<string>` (`:1`).
- **Concept introduced: two-factor state read through a capability interface, not the concrete `User`.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses interface segregation: a shared handler that needs to know whether TOTP is enrolled never needs the rest of the app's `User` shape, so it depends on this narrow contract instead. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses the shape of the stored secret itself: `TwoFactorSecret` (`:37`) is nullable, meaning "no enrollment started" is representable without a sentinel value, and it is never the plaintext Base32 key: it holds the protected form the framework handed the store (`:32-36`), so a read of the users table does not yield a working authenticator seed. `TwoFactorRecoveryCodeHashes` (`:43`) likewise holds hashes, not the plaintext codes a user was shown once at generation time.
- **Walkthrough**: `bool IsTwoFactorEnabled` (`:30`) gates whether a code is demanded at sign-in. `string? TwoFactorSecret` (`:37`) is the protected shared secret, `null` until enrollment begins; the protection is applied by [ITwoFactorSecretProtector](#itwofactorsecretprotector) before the secret reaches the store (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/TwoFactor/BeginTwoFactorEnrollmentHandlerBase.cs:28`, `:44`; the store contract repeats it at `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/TwoFactor/ITwoFactorStore.cs:42`). `IReadOnlyCollection<string> TwoFactorRecoveryCodeHashes` (`:43`) is empty both before enrollment and after every recovery code has been spent, which the doc comment (`:40-41`) states is a state the user recovers from by regenerating rather than an error condition.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping this state on its own interface, separate from [IAuthUser](#iauthuser) and [IPasswordChangeableUser](#ipasswordchangeableuser), lets an app opt into two-factor without every existing `User` aggregate needing new members it never populates. See [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html) for the opt-in model this interface belongs to.
- **Where it's used**: the generic constraint on [BeginTwoFactorEnrollmentHandlerBase<TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#begintwofactorenrollmenthandlerbasetcommand) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/TwoFactor/BeginTwoFactorEnrollmentHandlerBase.cs:65`, `:80`, where a missing state is reported as `NotFound` targeting this interface), and it is the state [ITwoFactorStore](#itwofactorstore) returns from `GetAsync` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/TwoFactor/ITwoFactorStore.cs:34`) against the concrete `User`. MMCA.Store's `User` lists it among its capability interfaces (`MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.Store.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:30`), and [AuditTrailSaveChangesInterceptor](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#audittrailsavechangesinterceptor) reads it to redact the two-factor material from audit rows.

### IAuthUser
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IAuthUser.cs:15` · Level 0 · interface

- **What it is**: the deliberately minimal **credential** surface an Identity module's `User` aggregate exposes to the shared [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser) workflow. Two properties of password material, plus one defaulted flag that marks a machine client's service account. It is the contract that lets the framework's authentication plumbing verify and replace a password without knowing anything app-specific about the user (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IAuthUser.cs:3-8`).
- **Depends on**: nothing first-party; the BCL only (`byte[]`). Implemented transitively through [IPasswordChangeableUser](#ipasswordchangeableuser) by each app's `User` aggregate (see [User](group-24-identity-module.md#user)).
- **Concept introduced: the inverted user contract.** Rather than the shared auth workflow depending on a concrete `User` class, `User` implements a small interface the framework owns. Profile fields, roles, linked aggregates, and claim sources stay app-specific: the shared workflow reaches those only through per-app hooks (`CreateAccessToken`, `CreateUser`), never through this contract (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IAuthUser.cs:6-8`). `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses interface segregation and dependency inversion, and this is a textbook case: the interface is exactly the credential surface and nothing more. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses credential handling, and the whole security-relevant surface of a `User` aggregate is readable in a dozen lines.
- **Concept: what the contract deliberately leaves out.** The `<para>` block (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IAuthUser.cs:9-13`) records what is deliberately **absent**: refresh tokens. They are rows in [RefreshSession](#refreshsession), one per signed-in device, hashed at rest and reached through [IRefreshSessionStore](#irefreshsessionstore), so no usable bearer credential sits in the users table and this interface covers passwords only ([ADR-097](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/097-multi-device-refresh-sessions.html)). `[Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality]` applies: documenting an absence on the contract itself stops a later change from "helpfully" putting a token column back on the user.
- **Walkthrough**: three members, all read-only.
  - `byte[] PasswordHash` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IAuthUser.cs:19`), the PBKDF2 hash produced by [IPasswordHasher](#ipasswordhasher), documented as either the versioned shape or the header-less legacy shape (`:18`, [ADR-032](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/032-password-hashing.html), [ADR-133](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/133-versioned-password-hash-work-factor.html)).
  - `byte[] PasswordSalt` (`:22`), the salt paired with it.
  - Both sit inside a scoped `#pragma warning disable CA1819` (`:17`, restored on `:23`) that knowingly returns arrays, to mirror [IPasswordHasher](#ipasswordhasher)'s `byte[]` tuple and the EF-mapped `varbinary` columns rather than force a defensive copy on every read. The suppression's justification is written on the disable line itself, which is the convention this codebase uses everywhere it takes an analyzer exception.
  - `bool IsServiceAccount => false` (`:32`) is a **default interface member** marking the service account behind a machine client rather than a person ([ADR-140](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/140-machine-clients-oauth-client-credentials.html)). Its doc comment (`:25-31`) states the policy: such an account obtains tokens only through the client-credentials grant, so password sign-in, sign-in links, external login and passkeys refuse it, and it can never be viewed as. The `false` default means an app that has not adopted machine clients implements nothing.
  - There is no mutator. Writing new material is the separate capability [IPasswordChangeableUser](#ipasswordchangeableuser) adds, so an aggregate that only ever authenticates never exposes a way to change its own password.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the contract in Domain and keeping it small is what makes the shared auth workflow reusable across Store and ADC (both `User` aggregates satisfy it) while each aggregate stays free to model everything else its own way. See [ADR-032](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/032-password-hashing.html) for the password-material policy, [ADR-004](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/004-authentication-dual-fetch.html) for the dual-fetch auth model this contract feeds, and [ADR-097](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/097-multi-device-refresh-sessions.html) for the refresh-token move.
- **Where it's used**: it is half the generic constraint on the shared login and registration workflow, `where TUser : AuditableAggregateRootEntity<UserIdentifierType>, IAuthUser` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:82`), which passes both password properties to `VerifyPassword` on the login path (`:212`) and refuses a service account on its sign-in branches (`:566`, `:612`, `:942`). It is also the base of [IPasswordChangeableUser](#ipasswordchangeableuser), and the shape hand-written test doubles copy. ADC's `User` overrides the flag with a stored `IsServiceAccount { get; private set; }` (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:145`, set to `true` only when a service account is provisioned, `:373`), and [ViewAsService](#viewasservice) refuses to view one (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsService.cs:178-180`, `ViewAs.TargetIsServiceAccount`).

### IPasswordChangeableUser
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IPasswordChangeableUser.cs:11` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the password-rotation surface an Identity module's `User` aggregate exposes to the shared [ChangePasswordHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#changepasswordhandlerbasetuser-tcommand) workflow. It is one method on top of [IAuthUser](#iauthuser) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IPasswordChangeableUser.cs:5-9`).
- **Depends on**: [IAuthUser](#iauthuser) (its base interface, `:11`) and [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`:1`).
- **Concept: capability interfaces layered by workflow.** `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses interface segregation, and this is the pattern applied twice over: a `User` that only ever authenticates satisfies [IAuthUser](#iauthuser); a `User` whose app offers self-service password change implements this one and gets `PasswordHash` and `PasswordSalt` along with it, because the workflow must verify the current credential before writing the new one (the XML comment states exactly this reason, `:7-9`). Inheritance here encodes a real dependency between capabilities rather than a taxonomy. `[Rubric §4, DDD]` also applies: the method returns [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result), so the aggregate can refuse the change (an invariant failure) instead of the handler assuming success.
- **Walkthrough**: one member, `Result ChangePassword(byte[] newPasswordHash, byte[] newPasswordSalt)` (`:19`). The aggregate receives already-hashed material, never a plaintext password: hashing is the handler's job via [IPasswordHasher](#ipasswordhasher), so no plaintext ever reaches the Domain layer or an EF change tracker.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the hash-and-salt pair as the parameter shape mirrors [IAuthUser](#iauthuser)'s two properties and [IPasswordHasher](#ipasswordhasher)'s tuple return, so the whole chain from handler to aggregate speaks one vocabulary. See [ADR-032](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/032-password-hashing.html).
- **Where it's used**: as the generic constraint `where TUser : AuditableAggregateRootEntity<UserIdentifierType>, IPasswordChangeableUser` on the shared change-password workflow (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/ChangePassword/ChangePasswordHandlerBase.cs:62`), which verifies the current password (`:55`), hashes the new one (`:61`), and calls `ChangePassword` with the result (`:62`). The forgot-password sibling, [ResetPasswordHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#resetpasswordhandlerbasetuser-tcommand), calls the same member on the redeem path after [IPasswordResetTokenService](#ipasswordresettokenservice) has identified the account (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/ResetPassword/ResetPasswordHandlerBase.cs:110-111`). Both apps' [User](group-24-identity-module.md#user) aggregates declare it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:37-38`, `MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.Store.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:29-30`), which is also how they pick up [IAuthUser](#iauthuser).

### IPasswordRehashableUser
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IPasswordRehashableUser.cs:16` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the opt-in surface that lets the shared [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser) sign-in flow upgrade a stored password hash to the hasher's current format and work factor while it still holds the verified plaintext. An Identity module's `User` that does not implement it keeps its stored hash exactly as it is (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IPasswordRehashableUser.cs:5-9`).
- **Depends on**: [IAuthUser](#iauthuser) (its base interface, `:16`, which supplies the `PasswordHash` the sign-in flow inspects) and [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`:1`).
- **Concept introduced: a re-derivation is not a password change.** The `<para>` block (`:10-14`) is the reason this interface exists beside [IPasswordChangeableUser](#ipasswordchangeableuser) rather than reusing its `ChangePassword`: a rehash keeps the same password, so it must not raise the aggregate's password-changed domain event, or anything else a real change triggers, such as revoking sessions or notifying the owner. `[Rubric §1, SOLID]` assesses interface segregation, and here two members with the same parameter shape are kept apart because their side effects differ. `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses credential storage over time: a hash written under an older work factor stays at that cost until something re-derives it, and the only moment the plaintext is available to do so is a successful sign-in ([ADR-133](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/133-versioned-password-hash-work-factor.html)).
- **Walkthrough**: one member, `Result RehashPassword(byte[] newPasswordHash, byte[] newPasswordSalt)` (`:25`), documented as replacing the stored material with a re-derivation of the same password without raising a password-changed event (`:18-21`). Like `ChangePassword` it receives already-hashed material, never the plaintext, and returns success or the aggregate's invariant failure (`:24`).
- **Why it's built this way**: the upgrade is opt-in twice over. The caller pattern-matches `user is not IPasswordRehashableUser rehashable` and returns when the aggregate does not implement it (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:1006`), and [IPasswordHasher](#ipasswordhasher)'s `NeedsRehash` is a default interface member that returns `false` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Interfaces/Infrastructure/Auth/IPasswordHasher.cs:28`), so a custom hasher that never overrides it never triggers a rewrite. The work runs after tokens are issued and saves on its own, so a refused invariant or a failed save cannot fail a sign-in that already succeeded (`AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:993-999`). See [ADR-032](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/032-password-hashing.html) for the password-material policy and [ADR-133](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/133-versioned-password-hash-work-factor.html) for the versioned work factor.
- **Where it's used**: `RehashPasswordIfNeededAsync` in [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser) is the only caller, invoked on the login path right after `IssueTokensAsync` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:295`). Inside a best-effort wrapper it checks `NeedsRehash` against the stored hash (`:688`), hashes the verified password (`:693`), calls `RehashPassword` (`:694`), logs `PasswordRehashRejected` through [AuthenticationServiceLog](#authenticationservicelog) on a refused invariant (`:697`), and otherwise saves through the unit of work (`:704`). The ADC [User](group-24-identity-module.md#user) aggregate implements it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:36`), validating the hash and salt with the same `UserInvariants` checks as a password change and assigning both without adding a domain event (`:442-457`), in contrast to `ChangePassword`, which raises `UserPasswordChanged` (`:429`). The MMCA.Store `User` implements it too (`MMCA.Store/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.Store.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:30`). The flow is covered by `AuthenticationServicePasswordRehashTests` (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Core/MMCA.Common.Application.Tests/Auth/AuthenticationServicePasswordRehashTests.cs`).

### IUserPreferences
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IUserPreferences.cs:10` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the stored UI-preference surface an Identity module's `User` aggregate exposes to the shared preference read and write workflows: preferred culture, preferred theme, and a single method that replaces both (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IUserPreferences.cs:5-8`).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`:1`). Nothing else; it is deliberately not tied to [IAuthUser](#iauthuser), because preferences are orthogonal to credentials.
- **Concept: null as "not chosen".** `[Rubric §27, i18n]` assesses whether locale is a first-class, persisted user choice rather than a per-session guess, and `[Rubric §19, State Management]` assesses where such UI state lives. Both properties are nullable, and the contract states that `null` means the user has not chosen that preference (`:7-8`), which is what lets the UI fall back to a browser or host default without needing a separate "is set" flag. See [ADR-027](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/027-multi-locale-i18n.html) for the culture model and [ADR-028](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/028-dark-theme-mode.html) for the theme model.
- **Walkthrough**: `string? PreferredCulture` (for example `"es"`, `:13`) and `string? PreferredTheme` (`"light"` or `"dark"`, `:16`) are read-only. `Result UpdatePreferences(string? preferredCulture, string? preferredTheme)` (`:25`) replaces **both** at once. The subtlety is documented at `:18-21`: because the method is a whole-object replace, the shared workflow always passes the currently stored value for any field the request left `null`, so writing one preference never silently clears the other. That read-then-merge is visible in the caller (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/ChangePreferences/ChangePreferencesHandlerBase.cs:52`).
- **Why it's built this way**: one replace method keeps the aggregate's invariant check in a single place, and pushing the merge into the workflow keeps the null-means-unchanged policy out of every app's `User`. Returning [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) lets the aggregate reject an unsupported culture or theme value.
- **Where it's used**: the read workflow constrains `where TUser : AuditableBaseEntity<UserIdentifierType>, IUserPreferences` and projects both properties into a response (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/GetPreferences/GetUserPreferencesHandlerBase.cs:21`, `:44`); the write workflow constrains `where TUser : AuditableAggregateRootEntity<UserIdentifierType>, IUserPreferences` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Users/UseCases/ChangePreferences/ChangePreferencesHandlerBase.cs:25`). Both are cross-linked as [GetUserPreferencesHandlerBase<TUser>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#getuserpreferenceshandlerbasetuser) and [ChangePreferencesHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#changepreferenceshandlerbasetuser-tcommand), and both apps' [User](group-24-identity-module.md#user) aggregates implement the interface.

### IEmailConfirmableUser
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IEmailConfirmableUser.cs:22` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the email-confirmation surface an Identity module's `User` aggregate exposes: whether the address has been proved, and a method that marks it confirmed (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/IEmailConfirmableUser.cs:24-32`).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions`.
- **Concept introduced: idempotent confirmation by contract.** `[Rubric §4, DDD]` assesses whether an aggregate enforces its own invariants rather than trusting the caller, and `ConfirmEmail()`'s doc comment (`:26-30`) states the requirement directly: implementations should be idempotent, so redeeming a second token for an address that is already confirmed is an ordinary duplicate outcome, not a fault. That reading matters because a user can legitimately click an old confirmation link twice (a second tab, a forwarded email), and the workflow must not turn that into an error.
- **Walkthrough**: `bool IsEmailConfirmed` (`:24`) is the current state. `Result ConfirmEmail()` (`:32`) returns a success result, or the aggregate's own invariant failure, and takes no parameters: the token itself is verified upstream by [IEmailConfirmationTokenService](#iemailconfirmationtokenservice) before this method is ever called.
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping confirmation as its own capability interface, alongside [ITwoFactorUserState](#itwofactoruserstate) and [IUserPreferences](#iuserpreferences), lets an app that does not require email confirmation skip implementing it, consistent with the opt-in model of [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html).
- **Where it's used**: the generic constraint on [SendEmailConfirmationHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#sendemailconfirmationhandlerbasetuser-tcommand) and [ConfirmEmailHandlerBase<TUser, TCommand>](group-14-module-system-composition.md#confirmemailhandlerbasetuser-tcommand), and by [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser), which reads `IsEmailConfirmed` on the login path.

### ILegalAcceptingUser
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/ILegalAcceptingUser.cs:21` · Level 3 · interface

- **What it is**: the terms-acceptance surface an Identity module's `User` aggregate exposes: which terms version the user last accepted, when, and a method that records a new acceptance (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/ILegalAcceptingUser.cs:21-38`).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions`. Nothing else; like [IUserPreferences](#iuserpreferences) it is not tied to [IAuthUser](#iauthuser).
- **Concept: idempotent acceptance by contract.** `[Rubric §4, DDD]` assesses whether an aggregate enforces its own invariants, and the `AcceptTerms` doc comment states that implementations should be idempotent for the same version: accepting the version already on record is an ordinary repeat, not a fault (`:34-37`). This mirrors [IEmailConfirmableUser](#iemailconfirmableuser), so a double-submitted acceptance form does not surface as an error.
- **Walkthrough**: `string? AcceptedTermsVersion` (`:29`) and `DateTime? TermsAcceptedOn` (`:32`, UTC) are read-only and `null` when the user never accepted. `Result AcceptTerms(string version, DateTime acceptedOn)` (`:42`) takes a non-blank version and the UTC instant, and returns success or the aggregate's invariant failure.
- **Why it's built this way**: a separate capability interface lets an app that does not gate on legal terms skip it, consistent with the opt-in model of [ADR-116](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/116-identity-completions-opt-in.html). The clock is passed in rather than read inside the aggregate, so the caller owns time.
- **Where it's used**: [AuthenticationServiceBase<TUser>](#authenticationservicebasetuser) documents the `user.AcceptTerms(CurrentTermsVersion, now)` call on an `ILegalAcceptingUser` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/AuthenticationServiceBase.cs:136`), and [ILegalAcceptanceService](#ilegalacceptanceservice) names it as the typical aggregate shape (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/Legal/ILegalAcceptanceService.cs:8`). The ADC [User](group-24-identity-module.md#user) aggregate implements it (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Identity/MMCA.ADC.Identity.Domain/Users/User.cs:38`).

### PasskeyCredential
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/PasskeyCredential.cs:20` · Level 3 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: one registered passkey, a WebAuthn public-key credential bound to one account: the public half of a key pair whose private half never leaves the user's authenticator (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/PasskeyCredential.cs:5-7`, [ADR-139](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/139-passkeys-webauthn-opt-in-sign-in.html)).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`:1`) and the `UserIdentifierType` alias. Persisted through [IPasskeyCredentialStore](#ipasskeycredentialstore) by [EFPasskeyCredentialStore](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#efpasskeycredentialstore), mapped by [PasskeyCredentialModelBuilderExtensions](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#passkeycredentialmodelbuilderextensions), and driven by [PasskeyService](#passkeyservice).
- **Concept introduced: a stored credential that is not a secret.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses what a database read yields. The class comment (`:15-17`) states it plainly: the credential id and the public key only verify signatures, so a dump of this table cannot sign anyone in, which is why neither is hashed the way [RefreshSession](#refreshsession) hashes its token. What this row must protect against instead is a **cloned authenticator**, and the signature counter is the tool: `IsSignCountAcceptable(long stored, uint presented)` (`:123-124`) accepts a counter that goes up, or zero on both sides (an authenticator that does not count, which is what synced passkeys do, `:52-55`), and refuses one that stays put or goes down, because that means two copies of the key are in use.
- **Concept: framework bookkeeping, not an aggregate.** Like [RefreshSession](#refreshsession), it is a flat record with no audit stamps, no soft-delete flag and no concurrency token: inserted at registration, touched on each sign-in, renamed, and deleted outright (`:9-13`). It is mapped only where a host opts in (`AddPasskeys` with `Passkeys:Enabled`), in the Identity database alone (`:12-13`), consistent with [ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **Width constants** published for the EF mapping: `CredentialIdMaxLength = 1023` (the longest id WebAuthn allows, `:23`), `PublicKeyMaxLength = 2048` (an RSA-4096 COSE key fits, `:26`), `NameMaxLength = 100` (`:29`), `TransportsMaxLength = 100` (`:32`), and `DefaultName = "Passkey"` (`:35`).
  - **State**: `Id` defaults to a fresh `Guid` and is what rename and delete address (`:38`); `UserId` is `required` (`:41`). `CredentialId` and `PublicKey` are `required byte[]` (`:45`, `:48`) inside a scoped `#pragma warning disable CA1819` (`:43-49`) whose justification cites EF's `varbinary` shape and the [IAuthUser](#iauthuser) precedent. `SignCount` (`:55`), `Name` (`:64`) and `LastUsedOn` (`:70`) have private setters; `Transports` (`:61`) holds comma-separated hints such as `internal` or `hybrid`, and `CreatedOn` (`:67`) is init-only.
  - **`Create(...)`** (`:83`) returns `Result<PasskeyCredential>`. It rejects an empty or oversized credential id (`Passkeys.CredentialIdInvalid`) or public key (`Passkeys.PublicKeyInvalid`) and a name over 100 characters (`ValidateMaterial`, `:163`), copies both byte arrays so the caller's buffers cannot mutate the row (`:105-106`), and turns a blank name into `DefaultName` (`:109`). Transport hints are best effort: an empty or oversized list is dropped to `null` rather than refusing the passkey (`:182-187`).
  - **`RecordUse(uint presentedSignCount, DateTime usedOn)`** (`:133`) applies the counter rule and returns `Passkeys.SignCountInvalid` as an `Unauthorized` error (`:137-140`) without touching the row, otherwise stores the new counter and the instant.
  - **`Rename(string? name)`** (`:151`) trims and requires 1 to 100 characters, failing with `Passkeys.NameInvalid` (`:189-190`).
- **Why it's built this way**: keeping the counter rule as a static pure function on the Domain type lets the sign-in path and the tests evaluate it without a row, while `RecordUse` guarantees the rule is applied before any write. Validation lives in the factory so an oversized value surfaces as a `[Rubric §4, DDD]`-shaped `Result` failure instead of a database constraint violation.
- **Where it's used**: [PasskeyService](#passkeyservice) creates the row after a verified registration (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/Passkeys/PasskeyService.cs:100`), renames it (`:137`) and records each sign-in (`:266`). ADC's Identity database carries the table through the `AddPasskeyCredentials` migration (`MMCA.ADC/Source/Hosting/MMCA.ADC.Migrations.SqlServer.Identity/Migrations/20261112192534_AddPasskeyCredentials.Designer.cs`). The rules are covered by `PasskeyCredentialTests` (`MMCA.Common/Tests/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain.Tests/Auth/PasskeyCredentialTests.cs`).

### PermissionGrant
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/PermissionGrant.cs:24` · Level 3 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: one row granting a single `area:capability` permission to a single role, with an audit trail of when and by whom it was created (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/PermissionGrant.cs:24-94`).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error), both from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions`. Persisted through [IPermissionGrantStore](#ipermissiongrantstore) and its EF adapter, and read into [IPermissionCatalog](#ipermissioncatalog)/[IPermissionRegistry](#ipermissionregistry) at runtime.
- **Concept introduced: two comparison conventions pinned by comment, not by type.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses authorization correctness, and this class carries the two rules an authorization decision depends on directly on the properties: `Role` (`:188`) is compared case-insensitively everywhere it is read, matching `PermissionRegistry` and `RoleValue`; `Permission` (`:194`) is compared ordinally, matching the compiled registry. Getting either comparison wrong would make a grant silently not match the token it was meant to authorize.
- **Walkthrough**: `RoleMaxLength = 64` (`:176`) and `PermissionMaxLength = 128` (`:179`) are published column widths. `Id` (`:182`) defaults to a fresh `Guid`. `Role` and `Permission` (`:188`, `:194`) are `required init`-only strings. `GrantedAt` (`:197`) is `required`; `GrantedBy` (`:203`) is optional and documented as informational only, never part of an authorization decision, so a row written by a migration with no principal is still honored. `Create(string role, string permission, DateTime grantedAt, string? grantedBy = null)` (`:213-242`) is the only constructor path: it fails validation with `PermissionGrant.RoleInvalid` when the role is blank or over 64 characters (`:219-225`), and `PermissionGrant.PermissionInvalid` when the permission is blank or over 128 (`:227-233`), then trims both before storing.
- **Why it's built this way**: validating length and blankness in the factory rather than trusting the caller keeps an oversized or empty value from reaching the database as a constraint violation instead of a `[Rubric §4, DDD]`-shaped `Result` failure. Grouping the two comparison conventions on the type that stores the data, rather than leaving them implicit in the store or the registry, is what keeps every reader consistent.
- **Where it's used**: written and read by [EFPermissionGrantStore](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#efpermissiongrantstore) and [StoredPermissionRoleAdministrationService](#storedpermissionroleadministrationservice), mapped by [PermissionGrantModelBuilderExtensions](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#permissiongrantmodelbuilderextensions), and its `RoleMaxLength`/`PermissionMaxLength` constants are cited by [SetUserRolesRequestValidator](#setuserrolesrequestvalidator) and [SetRolePermissionsRequestValidator](#setrolepermissionsrequestvalidator) (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/Validation/AdministrationRequestValidators.cs:22-23`, `:41-42`) when validating admin requests that set roles or permissions.

### ViewAsGrant
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/ViewAsGrant.cs:18` · Level 3 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: one read-only view-as grant: a staff user was allowed to see the app as another account for a bounded time, for a stated reason. The row is itself the audit record of that access (there is no separate audit-event API), and it is what the viewed account's sign-in history shows as "Viewed by support" (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/ViewAsGrant.cs:6-9`, [ADR-137](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/137-read-only-view-as-support-access.html)).
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error) from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions` (`:1`), the `ViewAsGrantStatus` enum from `MMCA.Common.Shared.Auth.Responses` (`:2`), and the `UserIdentifierType` alias. Persisted through [IViewAsGrantStore](#iviewasgrantstore) by [EFViewAsGrantStore](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#efviewasgrantstore), mapped by [ViewAsGrantModelBuilderExtensions](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#viewasgrantmodelbuilderextensions), and issued by [ViewAsService](#viewasservice).
- **Concept introduced: a bounded, justified, recorded impersonation.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses support access to user data. Three limits are enforced in the factory, not left to the caller: a staff user cannot view as themselves (`ViewAs.Self`, `:109-113`); the reason must be 10 to 500 characters after trimming, so `"x"` cannot stand in for a justification (`ReasonMinLength`/`ReasonMaxLength`, `:21`, `:24`; `ViewAs.ReasonInvalid`, `:118-123`); and the lifetime is clamped to `MaxLifetime`, 15 minutes, whatever the access-token lifetime is (`:30`, clamp at `:126-129`). The grant's `Id` travels in the view-as token as its `vag` claim (`:33`), with `StaffUserId` as `act_sub` and `TargetUserId` as `sub` (`:36`, `:39`), so every request can be checked against a live row.
- **Concept: framework bookkeeping, not an aggregate.** Like [RefreshSession](#refreshsession), a flat record with no audit stamps, no soft-delete flag and no concurrency token: inserted, possibly ended once, and swept after the retention window. No global query filter may hide one from the per-request liveness check (`:11-15`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **Constants**: `ReasonMinLength = 10` (`:21`), `ReasonMaxLength = 500` (`:24`), `DisplayMaxLength = 256` (an email address fits, `:27`), `MaxLifetime = 15 minutes` (`:30`).
  - **State**: `Id` (`:33`), `StaffUserId` (`:36`), `TargetUserId` (`:39`), the `required` `Reason` (`:42`), `GrantedAt` and `ExpiresAt` (`:45`, `:48`) are init-only; `EndedAt` (`:51`), `StaffDisplay` (`:59`) and `TargetDisplay` (`:66`) have private setters.
  - **Two `Create` overloads**: the five-argument form (`:78`) records no display snapshot and forwards to the seven-argument form (`:100`), which also snapshots both parties' emails so the support access log stays readable without a user lookup. A non-positive or oversized lifetime becomes `MaxLifetime`, and `ExpiresAt = grantedAt + lifetime` (`:137`).
  - **`NormalizeDisplay(string?)`** (`:151`) is both the storage form and the search-needle form: trimmed, lower-cased character by character with the invariant culture (so a match does not depend on a database collation), cut to 256 characters, and `null` when blank.
  - **Lifecycle**: `IsActiveAt(now)` (`:172`) is "not ended and not expired"; `StatusAt(now)` (`:181`) derives `Ended`, `Live` or `Expired`; `End(now)` (`:193`) is `EndedAt ??= now`, so ending an ended grant changes nothing.
  - **Erasure**: `ForgetDisplayOf(userId)` (`:202`) blanks the erased account's email snapshot on whichever side (staff, viewed, or both) it sits, and keeps the ids and the reason, so the access stays on record without the personal data ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)).
- **Why it's built this way**: making the grant row the audit record, rather than writing a separate event, means the evidence of access and the thing that authorizes access cannot diverge. Clamping the lifetime on the Domain type keeps the 15-minute ceiling true even if a caller asks for more, and [ITokenService](#itokenservice)'s short-lived mint is capped at the same `MaxLifetime`.
- **Where it's used**: [ViewAsService](#viewasservice) validates a request with the five-argument factory (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsService.cs:76`), creates the snapshotting grant (`:99`), and answers the per-request liveness question through `IsActiveAt` (`:143`), which [ViewAsGuardMiddleware](group-12-api-hosting-mapping.md#viewasguardmiddleware) relies on. [ViewAsGrantLogQuery](#viewasgrantlogquery) folds its search needles with `NormalizeDisplay` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/ViewAs/ViewAsGrantLogQuery.cs:36`, `:41`); [EFViewAsGrantStore](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#efviewasgrantstore) runs `ForgetDisplayOf` during erasure (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Auth/EFViewAsGrantStore.cs:161`); and `ViewAsGrantsAdminControllerBase` projects `StatusAt` into the admin log (`MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.API/Controllers/Administration/ViewAsGrantsAdminControllerBase.cs:90`).

### RefreshSession
> MMCA.Common.Domain · `MMCA.Common.Domain.Auth` · `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/RefreshSession.cs:46` · Level 4 · class (sealed)

- **What it is**: one refresh-token session, meaning a single device's right to mint access tokens for one user, held as a **hash** of the issued refresh token. A user has as many rows as they have signed-in devices, so signing in on a phone no longer signs the same account out of a laptop (BR-205/206, `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/RefreshSession.cs:9-12`). It implements [IAnonymizable](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#ianonymizable) (`:39`) so the device metadata it captures has an erasure path.
- **Depends on**: [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) and [Error](group-01-result-error-handling.md#error) (`:5`), [PiiAttribute](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#piiattribute) (`:3`), [IAnonymizable](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#ianonymizable) (`:4`), the `UserIdentifierType` alias, and from the BCL `System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256`, `System.Text.Encoding`, and `Convert.ToHexString` (`:1-2`). Persisted by [EFRefreshSessionStore](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#efrefreshsessionstore) behind [IRefreshSessionStore](#irefreshsessionstore), mapped by [RefreshSessionModelBuilderExtensions](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#refreshsessionmodelbuilderextensions), swept by [RefreshSessionCleanupService](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#refreshsessioncleanupservice), tuned by [RefreshSessionSettings](#refreshsessionsettings).
- **Concept introduced: a refresh token is a credential, so store its digest and make reuse detectable.** `[Rubric §11, Security]` assesses how a long-lived credential is stored, rotated, and revoked, and this one class carries four separate properties that are each worth understanding on their own.
  - **Hash at rest.** The plaintext refresh token exists only in the response that hands it to the client; the row keeps `TokenHash` (`:72`), so a database read cannot mint tokens (`:14-16`). That forces one design consequence the comment calls out explicitly: because lookups are **by hash**, the digest must be unsalted and deterministic. A per-row salt would make the token unfindable. This is the opposite trade-off from [PasswordHasher](#passwordhasher), and legitimately so: a refresh token is 64 random bytes from a CSPRNG rather than a human-chosen password, so there is no dictionary to run against it and no value in slowing the digest down.
  - **Rotation leaves a chain.** Using a session revokes it and records its successor in `ReplacedByTokenHash` (`:19-22`, `:83-87`). The point is not bookkeeping: presenting an already-rotated token lands on a **revoked row** rather than on nothing, and that difference is the signal that a token was replayed. A stolen-and-replayed token therefore triggers revocation of the whole family instead of failing quietly (BR-206 reuse detection, [ADR-050](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/050-jwt-refresh-token-rotation.html)).
  - **Framework bookkeeping, not an aggregate.** The class comment (`:24-31`) is explicit that this is a flat record like [OutboxMessage](group-04-events-outbox.md#outboxmessage) and [AuditTrailEntry](group-07-persistence-ef-core.md#audittrailentry): no audit stamps, no soft-delete flag, no concurrency token. The reason matters for `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]`: rows are never deleted or edited except to be revoked, and **no global query filter may hide a revoked row**, because the reuse check depends on finding it. It is also mapped only where a consumer opts in (`ApplyRefreshSessionConfiguration`), since sessions belong to the Identity module's database rather than to every data source ([ADR-006](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/006-database-per-service.html) database-per-service).
  - **Personal data is separable from the credential.** The class comment (`:32-37`) splits the row in two: `IpAddress` and `UserAgent` identify the data subject's device and network, so both carry `[Pii]` and `Anonymize` clears them for an erasure request ([ADR-005](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/005-soft-delete-vs-erasure.html)), while the token hashes, timestamps and revocation chain carry no personal data and are kept. That split is what lets reuse detection keep working on an anonymized row. It also satisfies the framework's PII convention, under which any domain entity with a `[Pii]`-marked property must implement `IAnonymizable` (`MMCA.Common/Source/Hosting/MMCA.Common.Testing.Architecture/Rules/Governance/ArchitectureRules.Governance.cs:10`).
- **Walkthrough**
  - **Width and reason constants** (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Domain/Auth/RefreshSession.cs:49-79`): `TokenHashLength = 64` (the width of a hex-encoded SHA-256 digest, `:46`), `IpAddressMaxLength = 45` (sized to fit an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal, `:49`), `UserAgentMaxLength = 512` (`:52`), `ReasonRevokedMaxLength = 64` (`:55`), and the five revocation reasons `ReasonRotated` (`:58`), `ReasonSignedOut` (`:61`), `ReasonReuseDetected` (`:64`), `ReasonSessionCap` (`:67`, value `"SessionCapExceeded"`), and `ReasonAccountDeleted` (`:70`, value `"AccountDeleted"`, recorded when a session is revoked because its account was deleted and erased). Publishing the widths as `public const` on the Domain type is what lets the EF configuration derive every column width from the same numbers (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Infrastructure/Persistence/Auth/RefreshSessionModelBuilderExtensions.cs:52`, `:52`, `:56-58`) rather than repeating magic numbers in a mapping file.
  - **State** (`:73-112`): `Id` defaults to a fresh `Guid` (`:73`); `UserId`, `TokenHash`, `CreatedAt` and `ExpiresAt` are `required` and `init`-only (`:76-85`), so a session cannot be constructed without them and cannot be rewritten afterwards. Three revocation members carry `private set` and change only through `Revoke`: `RevokedAt` (`:88`), `ReplacedByTokenHash` (`:94`), `ReasonRevoked` (`:97`). `IpAddress` (`:105`) and `UserAgent` (`:112`) are optional capture, each marked `[Pii]` (`:104`, `:111`) and also `private set`: they are written once by `Create` and afterwards only cleared by `Anonymize`, never set from outside. The `UserAgent` comment (`:100-103`) gives the reason for its marking: alongside the IP it fingerprints the data subject's device. The comment on `IpAddress` (`:92-96`) is a good example of documenting what a field is **not** for: it identifies a session in a "your devices" list and gives an audit trail for a revocation, and it is never part of a validation decision, so a mobile client changing networks is not signed out.
  - **Derived state**: `IsRevoked => RevokedAt is not null` (`:115`) and `IsActiveAt(DateTime utcNow) => !IsRevoked && ExpiresAt > utcNow` (`:119`). Passing the instant in rather than reading a clock keeps the type free of ambient time, which is what makes it directly unit-testable (see [RefreshSessionTests](group-29-testing-infrastructure.md#per-project-test-rollup)).
  - **`Create(...)`** (`:132-165`), the factory returning `Result<RefreshSession>` in the framework's standard shape (see the primer on factory methods and the [Result](group-01-result-error-handling.md#result) pattern). Two guards: a blank token fails with `RefreshSession.TokenRequired` (`:140-146`), and an expiry at or before creation fails with `RefreshSession.ExpiryInPast` (`:148-154`), both `Error.Validation`. On success it hashes the token on the way in (`:159`), so **the plaintext never reaches a property**, and truncates the two optional capture fields to their column widths (`:162-163`). Truncating in the factory rather than trusting the caller is what keeps an oversized `User-Agent` header from turning a login into a database error.
  - **`HashToken(string refreshToken)`** (`:180-184`): `Convert.ToHexString(SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(refreshToken)))`, guarded by `ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace` (`:182`). The `<remarks>` (`:171-177`) is the one piece of this file to read twice: the encoding is **part of the contract, not an implementation detail**, because a consumer's data migration has to reproduce it exactly to carry existing tokens over. It even gives the T-SQL equivalent, `CONVERT(char(64), HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', CONVERT(varchar(max), Token)), 2)`, and explains both halves of why it matches: style 2 emits upper-case hex with no `0x` prefix, and the `varchar` conversion is what makes the hashed bytes UTF-8 rather than SQL Server's default UTF-16. `[Rubric §8, Data Architecture]` and `[Rubric §34, Architecture Governance & Documentation]` both apply here: a hash format that a migration must reproduce is a published contract, and it is documented as one.
  - **`Revoke(DateTime revokedAt, string reason, string? replacedByTokenHash = null)`** (`:194-209`): the only mutator of session state. It is **idempotent by refusal** (`:187-188`), returning `Error.Invariant("RefreshSession.AlreadyRevoked", ...)` when the session is already revoked (`:196-202`) rather than silently overwriting, so the first reason and instant recorded are the ones kept. That matters for forensics: a session revoked by reuse detection must not have that reason overwritten by a later sign-out or by the account-erasure step. On success it stamps the instant, the truncated reason, and the successor hash (`:204-206`).
  - **`Anonymize()`** (`:217-222`): the [IAnonymizable](group-02-domain-building-blocks.md#ianonymizable) member. It nulls `IpAddress` and `UserAgent` and returns `Result.Success()`. Unlike `Revoke` it is **idempotent by acceptance** (`:211-215`): an already-anonymized session stays as it is and the call still succeeds, because erasing absent data is not an error. It deliberately leaves the session's validity untouched; revoking is the sign-out path's job, so anonymizing a row and ending it remain two separate decisions.
  - `Truncate` (`:224-225`) is the shared private helper, returning the value unchanged when it is null, empty, or already short enough.
- **Why it's built this way**: [ADR-097](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/097-multi-device-refresh-sessions.html) records the move from one plaintext refresh-token column on the user row to a session table, and [ADR-050](https://ivanball.github.io/docs/adr/050-jwt-refresh-token-rotation.html) the rotation-and-reuse-detection model the chain implements. Keeping the class free of audit stamps and soft-delete is deliberate rather than an omission, and keeping `Create`/`Revoke`/`Anonymize` as the only ways in and out means every row in the table was validated, every revoked row carries a reason, and personal data can be erased without breaking the chain.
- **Where it's used**: [AuthSessionIssuer](#authsessionissuer) is the main consumer. It hashes a presented token to look the session up (`MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/Sessions/AuthSessionIssuer.cs:200`, `:285`), creates one per login (`:320`) and per rotation (`:360`), revokes on sign-out (`:166`, `:172`, `:180`) and on a by-id revoke from the device list (`:247`), revokes the live family on reuse detection (`:295`, `:383`), and evicts the oldest session with `ReasonSessionCap` when a user is at `RefreshSessions:MaxActiveSessionsPerUser` (`:427`, documented at `:409`; default 10 at `MMCA.Common/Source/Core/MMCA.Common.Application/Auth/RefreshSessionSettings.cs:35`).
